title: Python Programming
description: Python basics: types, control flow, functions, collections, strings, classes and exceptions.

questions.prompt: Which function prints output to the console in Python 3?
questions.explanation: print() writes its arguments to standard output.

questions.prompt: Which symbol starts a single-line comment in Python?
questions.explanation: Everything after # on a line is a comment.

questions.prompt: How does Python mark a block of code?
questions.explanation: Python uses consistent indentation to define blocks.

questions.prompt: What does type(3.0) return?
questions.explanation: 3.0 is a floating-point literal, so its type is float.

questions.prompt: What is 7 // 2 in Python 3?
questions.explanation: // is floor division, giving 3.

questions.prompt: What is 7 / 2 in Python 3?
questions.explanation: / is true division and always returns a float, here 3.5.

questions.prompt: Which of these types is immutable?
questions.explanation: Tuples cannot be changed after creation; lists, dicts and sets can.

questions.prompt: What is bool([])?
questions.explanation: Empty containers are falsy, so bool([]) is False.

questions.prompt: Which keyword adds another condition after if?
questions.explanation: Python spells it elif.

questions.prompt: What does print(10 > 5 and 3 > 4) output?
questions.explanation: 10 > 5 is True but 3 > 4 is False, so and gives False.

questions.prompt: Which operator tests whether two values are equal?
questions.explanation: == compares values; = assigns.

questions.prompt: What does range(3) produce?
questions.explanation: range(n) starts at 0 and stops before n.

questions.prompt: What does break do inside a loop?
questions.explanation: break leaves the nearest enclosing loop immediately.

questions.prompt: What does continue do inside a loop?
questions.explanation: continue jumps to the next iteration of the loop.

questions.prompt: Which keyword defines a function?
questions.explanation: Functions are defined with def.

questions.prompt: What does a function return if it has no return statement?
questions.explanation: Without an explicit return, a function returns None.

questions.prompt: What is *args used for in a function definition?
choices: Accepting any number of positional arguments
questions.explanation: *args collects extra positional arguments into a tuple.

questions.prompt: After def f(x=[]): x.append(1); return x, what does f(); print(f()) print?
questions.explanation: The default list is created once and shared between calls, so the second call returns [1, 1].

questions.prompt: How do you access the first element of list a?
questions.explanation: Python lists are zero-indexed.

questions.prompt: What does a.append(x) do?
choices: Adds x to the end of the list
questions.explanation: append modifies the list in place by adding x at the end.
Negative indices count from the end; -1 is the last element.

questions.prompt: How do you read the value stored under key 'k' in dict d?
questions.explanation: Use square brackets with the key: d['k'].

questions.prompt: Which describes a Python set?
questions.explanation: A set stores unique items without a defined order.

questions.prompt: What does d.get('x', 0) return when 'x' is not a key of d?
questions.explanation: get returns the supplied default, here 0, instead of raising KeyError.

questions.prompt: What is 'hello'[1:3]?
questions.explanation: Slicing includes index 1 and excludes index 3, giving 'el'.

questions.prompt: Which string method returns an uppercase copy?
questions.explanation: str.upper() returns the string in uppercase.

questions.prompt: Which method is normally used to initialise a new object's attributes?
questions.explanation: __init__ runs after an object is created to set up its attributes.

questions.prompt: What does self refer to inside an instance method?
questions.explanation: self is the instance the method was called on.

questions.prompt: Which block runs only when the try block raised no exception?
questions.explanation: The else clause of try runs only if no exception occurred.

questions.prompt: Which form opens a file so it is closed automatically?
questions.explanation: The with statement closes the file when the block ends, even after errors.

lessons.title: Python basics and syntax
lessons.body: Python uses indentation to define blocks and # for comments. Variables are created by assignment and need no declaration. print() writes to the console and input() reads a line of text as a string.

lessons.title: Numbers, booleans and type conversion
lessons.body: Core types are int, float, bool, str and None. / is true division and always gives a float, // is floor division and % is the remainder. Empty containers, 0, '' and None are falsy. Convert with int(), float(), str() and bool().

lessons.title: Mutable and immutable types
lessons.body: Lists, dicts and sets are mutable and can change in place. Strings, tuples, numbers and frozensets are immutable. Only immutable (hashable) objects can be dict keys or set members.

lessons.title: Conditionals: if, elif, else
lessons.body: Use if, elif and else to branch. Combine tests with and, or and not. == compares values and 'is' compares identity. Python allows chained comparisons such as 0 < x < 10.

lessons.title: Loops: for, while, range
lessons.body: for iterates over any iterable, while repeats as long as a condition holds. range(n) yields 0 to n-1. break exits a loop and continue skips to the next iteration. enumerate gives index and value together.

lessons.title: Functions, arguments and return values
lessons.body: Define functions with def. Parameters can have defaults, and *args and **kwargs collect extra positional and keyword arguments. Without a return statement a function returns None. Avoid mutable default values such as [] because they are shared between calls.

lessons.title: Lambda, map and comprehensions
lessons.body: A lambda is a small anonymous function. List comprehensions build lists concisely and are usually preferred over map and filter for readability.
lessons.example:
squares = [x * x for x in range(5)]
print(squares)  # [0, 1, 4, 9, 16]

lessons.title: Lists and tuples
lessons.body: Lists are ordered, mutable sequences; tuples are ordered and immutable. Indexing starts at 0 and negative indices count from the end. append adds to the end, insert adds at a position, pop removes and returns an item, and sort orders in place.

lessons.title: Dictionaries and sets
lessons.body: A dict maps keys to values. d[key] raises KeyError if the key is missing, while d.get(key, default) returns a default. A set stores unique, unordered items and supports fast membership tests and set operations such as union and intersection.

lessons.title: Strings and slicing
lessons.body: Strings are immutable sequences of characters. Slicing s[a:b] includes a and excludes b. Useful methods: upper, lower, strip, split, join and replace. f-strings embed expressions in text.

lessons.title: Classes and objects
lessons.body: A class defines attributes and methods. __init__ initialises a new instance and self refers to the instance a method is called on. Inheritance lets a subclass reuse and extend a parent class.

lessons.title: Exceptions and try/except
lessons.body: Wrap risky code in try and handle problems in except. else runs only when no exception occurred and finally always runs. Catch specific exceptions rather than a bare except, and use raise to signal errors.

lessons.title: Reading and writing files
lessons.body: Open files with the with statement so they close automatically, even if an error occurs. Modes include 'r' (read), 'w' (write, truncates) and 'a' (append).

lessons.title: Recursion in Python
lessons.body: A recursive function calls itself and needs a base case. Python limits recursion depth (about 1000 by default), so deep problems are better solved with loops.
lessons.example:
def fact(n):
    return 1 if n <= 1 else n * fact(n - 1)
